classes.name: Elección de Presidente y Vicepresidente de la República
classes.locator: https://www.impo.com.uy/bases/constitucion/1967-1967/151 (art. 151: "serán elegidos conjunta y directamente por el Cuerpo Electoral por mayoría absoluta de votantes")
classes.note: A joint ticket elected nationwide every five years. Until 1994 the presidency went to the most voted candidate of the most voted party (lema) by the double simultaneous vote, with several candidates per party; since the 1996 reform each party runs one ticket chosen in the primaries, and a ticket short of an absolute majority faces a runoff (segunda elección) on the last Sunday of November. Each round is its own contest. No election was held between 1971 and 1984 (dictatorship).

classes.name: Colegios Electorales de Senador
classes.name_en: Senators chosen by departmental electoral colleges (1830-1934)
classes.locator: https://www.impo.com.uy/bases/leyes-originales/7812-1925/3 (art. 3: "Colegios Electorales de Senador")
classes.note: Each department's voters elected a Colegio Elector, which then chose the department's senator; the Senate was renewed by thirds.
classes.disposition_reason: The popular votes elected only the departmental colleges; the Corte Electoral publishes no results for these college elections (its series starts in 1954), and they survive only in parliamentary and press records.

classes.name: Plebiscitos de reforma constitucional
classes.locator: https://www.impo.com.uy/bases/constitucion/1967-1967/331 (art. 331: proposals "sometidos al plebiscito en la primera elección que se realice"; approval needs a majority of at least 35% of registered voters)
classes.note: Constitutional reforms are put to the voters, usually on the day of the national election (a voter who does not put in the Sí ballot counts against); a reform from a constitutional law may go to a separate plebiscite (1980, 1994, 1996). Each proposal is one contest.

classes.name_en: Conaprole cooperative and OSE staff fund elections

classes.name: Designación de la Corte Electoral
classes.locator: https://www.impo.com.uy/bases/constitucion/1967-1967/324 (art. 324: nine members chosen by the General Assembly)
classes.disposition_reason: Chosen by the General Assembly, five by a two-thirds vote and four party representatives by double simultaneous vote; not by voters.

classes.name: Poder Judicial
classes.locator: https://www.impo.com.uy/bases/constitucion/1967-1967/236 (art. 236: Supreme Court members designated by the General Assembly)
classes.disposition_reason: No judge is elected by voters: the Supreme Court is chosen by the General Assembly and it appoints the other judges.

classes.name: Convenciones de los partidos
classes.disposition_reason: The national and departmental conventions elected in the primaries then choose presidential (when no precandidate wins outright) and intendant candidates by delegate vote; those are internal votes of elected delegates, not of voters.
